title: Which five lockers hold the code to the treasure?
description: The video finds the first five lockers that are touched by exactly two people, using the method of counting the factors of a locker number. It checks each locker found by listing its factors again.
teaching_notes: One idea: touched exactly twice means exactly two factors, one and the number itself. Watch for students who count locker one, which has a single factor, or locker four, which has three.

video_script.why: The child uses the factor counting of the solved example to find the lockers touched exactly twice, which are the primes.
video_script.substitution: Count the factors of each locker number from one upwards and keep those with exactly two factors.
video_script.anchor: the row of closed lockers of {{NAME_1}}, with the code lockers to be found
video_script.payoff_line: The code lockers are two, three, five, seven and eleven

final_answer.spoken: lockers two, three, five, seven and eleven

names.{{NAME_1}}: the queen of Khoisnam whose will hides the treasure in one of 100 lockers

never_show: the answer 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11 before the answer beat
maths_rules: a locker is touched by person k exactly when k divides its number, so touches = factors
touched exactly twice = exactly two factors: 1 and the number itself
numbers with exactly two factors: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, so these are the first five
check: 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11 each have only the factors 1 and the number itself
video_script.design: One idea: touched twice means two factors. The row of lockers stays in the anchor band; the factor list grows on the working board.

<bookmark mark='code'/>The first five lockers touched exactly twice hold the code to the treasure.

narration: <bookmark mark='touch'/>Use the same method as for locker twelve. A person touches a locker only if that number goes into it.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The number of touches is the number of factors.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the lockers are numbered one, two, three and so on.

beats.on_screen: To find: the first five lockers touched exactly twice

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the first five lockers touched exactly twice.

beats.on_screen: touched exactly twice = exactly two factors = 1 and the number itself

marks.two: the words exactly two factors are written
marks.which: the factors 1 and the number itself are marked

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step one, touched exactly twice means exactly two factors.
<bookmark mark='which'/>Those two can only be one and the number itself.

marks.list: the factors of lockers 2 to 6 appear one row at a time
marks.keep: the lockers with two factors get a tick

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step two, list the factors from locker one. Locker one has only one factor.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Two has one and two, three has one and three, and four has one, two and four.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>Five has one and five, but six has four factors.

marks.list: the factors of lockers 7 to 11 appear one row at a time
marks.name: the words prime number appear beside the ticked lockers

narration: <bookmark mark='list'/>Step three, carry on. Seven has two factors, but eight, nine and ten have more.
<bookmark mark='name'/>Eleven has two factors. A number with exactly two factors is called a prime number.

beats.on_screen: check: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 each have only 1 and itself

marks.check: each ticked locker is put back into the question and tested again

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, put the answer back in the question. Each of these lockers has only one and itself as factors, so each is touched twice.

marks.ans: the answer is boxed and the treasure box opens

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The code lockers are two, three, five, seven and eleven.
